narrative: OMX30 faces conflicting signals this morning: technicals remain solidly bullish with the index trading +4.2% above its 200-day MA, MACD above signal, and ADX showing strong trending momentum at 29.3. However, a -0.833% weighted correlation signal from yesterday's broad European selloff (DAX -1.17%, CAC -1.10%, FTSE -1.09%) combined with negative momentum from Asia (Nikkei -1.34%) suggests overnight positioning favors caution. US yields jumping 47bp to 5.145% creates a net-negative headwind for the 28% industrial weighting due to oil's +1.59% spike raising input costs, offsetting gains for the 18% banking sector from wider NIMs. The Deutsche Bank scandal creates systemic contagion risk in financial sentiment. While RSI at 58 and Stochastic neutral indicate no overbought compression, the technical strength appears vulnerable to correlation reversal if European risk-off persists.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens to headwinds from broad European selloff and negative correlation bias (-0.833%) despite solid technical structure. The index sits 93% through its 52-week range and +4.2% above 200-MA (key support at ~3085), but yesterday's coordinated weakness across DAX, CAC, and FTSE suggests modest downside bias into European cash open. Watch 3123 (yesterday close) as pivot; a break below 3110 targets the 50-MA at 3080. Industrials (28% weight: Volvo, Atlas Copco, Sandvik) face headwind from Brent +1.59% lifting input costs, partially offset by USD/SEK +0.54% export tailwind. Banks trade higher on 5.145% yields (NIM expansion), but Deutsche Bank scandal darkens sentiment. Avoid chasing on MACD strength until correlation signal stabilizes. Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET and any further Deutsche Bank escalation.
